title: Hypercube Adjacency
content: **hypercubeAdj n x y**: Two vertices $x, y \in \text{Fin}(2^n)$ of the $n$-dimensional hypercube are adjacent if and only if they differ in exactly one bit position. Formalized via $\exists! i : \text{Fin } n$ such that the $i$-th bits of $x$ and $y$ differ, where the $i$-th bit is extracted as $(x / 2^i) \bmod 2$. This captures the Hamming distance-1 condition using integer arithmetic rather than explicit binary strings.

title: Symmetry and Irreflexivity of Q_n
content: **hypercubeAdj_symm**: If $x \sim y$ in $Q_n$ then $y \sim x$, proved by applying `Ne.symm` to the bit-difference witness. **hypercubeAdj_irrefl**: No vertex is adjacent to itself, proved by contradiction since $x = y$ implies all bits agree, contradicting the existence of a differing bit. These two properties establish that `hypercubeAdj` defines a valid simple graph (symmetric and irreflexive).

title: Vertex and Edge Counts
content: **hypercube_vertex_count**: $|V(Q_n)| = 2^n$, proved directly via `Fintype.card_fin`. **hypercube_edge_count_formula**: The edge count satisfies $n \cdot 2^n / 2 = n \cdot 2^{n-1}$, proved by algebraic manipulation. Since each vertex has degree $n$ (one neighbor per bit flip), the handshaking lemma gives $|E(Q_n)| = n \cdot 2^n / 2 = n \cdot 2^{n-1}$.

title: Ramsey Number R(Q_n)
content: **ramseyNumber n**: The 2-color Ramsey number $R(Q_n)$, defined as $\inf\{N : \forall c : \text{Fin } N \to \text{Fin } N \to \text{Fin } 2, \exists f : \text{Fin}(2^n) \hookrightarrow \text{Fin } N \text{ injective}, \exists \text{color} \in \{0,1\}, \forall x \sim y \text{ in } Q_n, c(f(x), f(y)) = \text{color}\}$. This captures: for every edge-coloring of $K_N$, there is a monochromatic copy of $Q_n$ as an induced subgraph. Noncomputable due to `sInf`.

title: Base Case: R(Q_0) ≤ 1
content: **ramseyNumber_zero_bound**: $R(Q_0) \leq 1$, proved constructively. The 0-cube $Q_0$ has vertex set $\text{Fin}(2^0) = \text{Fin}(1)$, so it is a single vertex with no edges (by irreflexivity). Any 1-vertex graph trivially contains a monochromatic copy. The proof constructs the constant embedding $f(x) = 0$ and uses `hypercubeAdj_irrefl` to discharge the vacuous edge condition.
mathContext: $R(Q_0) \leq 1$ since $Q_0$ has one vertex and no edges

title: Burr-Erdős Conjecture for Hypercubes
content: **erdos_181_conjecture**: The main open problem. There exists $C > 0$ such that $R(Q_n) \leq C \cdot 2^n$ for all $n$, i.e., the Ramsey number of $Q_n$ is at most linear in its vertex count $2^n$. This would mean $R(Q_n) = O(2^n)$, making the trivial lower bound $R(Q_n) \geq 2^n$ essentially tight up to a constant factor. Axiomatized as an open conjecture.

title: Tikhomirov's Best Upper Bound (2022)
content: **tikhomirov_2022**: The current best upper bound $R(Q_n) \leq C \cdot 2^{(2-c)n}$ for constants $C > 0$ and $c > 0$ (with $c \approx 0.0366$ permissible). This is subquadratic in the vertex count $2^n$ (since the exponent $2-c < 2$) but still superlinear, leaving an exponent gap of $\approx 0.964$ with the conjectured linear bound. The proof uses the regularity method and probabilistic embedding techniques.

title: Trivial Lower Bound
content: **lower_bound**: $R(Q_n) \geq 2^n$ for $n \geq 1$. Since $Q_n$ has $2^n$ vertices, any monochromatic copy of $Q_n$ requires at least $2^n$ vertices in the host graph. Thus the complete graph $K_N$ with $N < 2^n$ cannot contain $Q_n$, regardless of the coloring. This is the simplest Ramsey lower bound: the vertex count.

title: Lee's Bounded-Degree Result (2017)
content: **lee_bounded_degree_ramsey**: Lee (2017) proved the Burr-Erdős conjecture for bounded-degree graphs: for every $\Delta$, there exists $C_\Delta > 0$ such that $R(G) \leq C_\Delta \cdot |V(G)|$ for all graphs $G$ with maximum degree $\leq \Delta$. However, $Q_n$ has degree $n \to \infty$, so Lee's result does not apply. Axiomatized in simplified form (the full formalization would require graph minor theory).

title: Bound Gap Illustration
content: **bound_gap_description**: Proves $2^n \leq 2^{2n}$ for all $n$, illustrating the exponent gap between the lower bound (exponent 1) and the trivial quadratic upper bound (exponent 2). The actual gap is between exponent 1 (conjectured) and exponent $2-c \approx 1.964$ (Tikhomirov). Proved via `Nat.pow_le_pow_right` and `omega`.
